title: Ezekiel Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 15.

questions.question: Who did the word of the LORD come to in Ezekiel 15:1?
options: Son of man
Moses
David
Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: Son of man
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying,' addressing the 'Son of man,' which refers to Ezekiel himself.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 15:2, what is compared to other trees of the forest?
options: The vine tree
The oak tree
The cedar tree
The olive tree
questions.correctAnswer: The vine tree
questions.explanation: Verse 2 specifically asks, 'What is the vine tree more than any tree, or than a branch which is among the trees of the forest?' indicating the vine tree is the focus.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 15:3, what is questioned about the wood from the vine tree?
options: If it can be used to make a pin
If it can produce fruit
If it can grow tall
If it can be used for building houses
questions.correctAnswer: If it can be used to make a pin
questions.explanation: The verse asks, 'Shall wood be taken thereof to do any work? or will men take a pin of it to hang any vessel thereon?' questioning its usefulness for making a pin.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 15:4 states that the wood of the vine tree is good for making vessels.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says the wood is cast into the fire for fuel and is burned entirely, implying it is not suitable for making vessels.

questions.question: What happens to the wood of the vine tree in Ezekiel 15:4?
options: It is cast into the fire for fuel
It is carved into statues
It is planted again
It is used to build houses
questions.correctAnswer: It is cast into the fire for fuel
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states, 'Behold, it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire devoureth both the ends of it, and the midst of it is burned.'

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 15:5 indicates that the vine tree was useful for work even before being burned.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says, 'when it was whole, it was meet for no work,' indicating it was not useful even before burning.

questions.question: What does the Lord GOD say He will do to the inhabitants of Jerusalem in Ezekiel 15:6?
options: Give them to the fire for fuel
Bless them with abundance
Lead them to a new land
Protect them from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Give them to the fire for fuel
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'As the vine tree among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so will I give the inhabitants of Jerusalem,' indicating judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 15:7, what will happen when the LORD sets His face against the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
options: They shall go out from one fire to another
They shall prosper and multiply
They shall build a temple
They shall find peace and rest
questions.correctAnswer: They shall go out from one fire to another
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says, 'they shall go out from one fire, and another fire shall devour them,' illustrating ongoing judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 15:8 declares that the land will be made desolate because of a trespass.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And I will make the land desolate, because they have committed a trespass,' confirming the reason for desolation.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 15:3, what is the rhetorical question asked about the wood of the vine tree?
options: Shall wood be taken thereof to do any work?
Will it bear more fruit than other trees?
Can it grow faster than other trees?
Is it the strongest wood in the forest?
questions.correctAnswer: Shall wood be taken thereof to do any work?
questions.explanation: The verse asks, 'Shall wood be taken thereof to do any work? or will men take a pin of it to hang any vessel thereon?' questioning its usefulness.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in Ezekiel 15 as a use for the vine tree wood?
options: To do any work
To make a pin
To hang a vessel
To build a house
questions.correctAnswer: To build a house
questions.explanation: The chapter questions its use for work, pins, or hanging vessels but does not mention building houses.

questions.question: True or False: The fire devours both ends and the midst of the vine tree wood according to Ezekiel 15:4.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 4 clearly states, 'the fire devoureth both the ends of it, and the midst of it is burned.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 15:5, is the vine tree wood fit for any work after being burned?
options: No, it is not fit for any work
Yes, it is still useful
Only for making pins
Only for hanging vessels
questions.correctAnswer: No, it is not fit for any work
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says, 'how much less shall it be meet yet for any work, when the fire hath devoured it, and it is burned?' indicating it is unfit after burning.

questions.question: What is the main metaphor used in Ezekiel 15 to describe the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
options: Vine tree given to fire for fuel
Oak tree standing tall
Cedar tree in the forest
Olive branch of peace
questions.correctAnswer: Vine tree given to fire for fuel
questions.explanation: Verse 6 compares the inhabitants to the vine tree given to the fire for fuel as a metaphor for judgment.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 15, which event occurs first?
options: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel
The land is made desolate
The inhabitants are given to fire
The fire devours the vine tree
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel
questions.explanation: Verse 1 begins with the word of the LORD coming to Ezekiel, which precedes other events in the chapter.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 15:4, what happens to the vine tree when it is cast into the fire?
options: It produces good fruit
The fire devours both the ends and the midst of it
It becomes strong and useful for work
It grows larger and more fruitful
questions.correctAnswer: The fire devours both the ends and the midst of it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4 states that when the vine tree is cast into the fire, the fire devours both the ends and the midst of it, indicating it is consumed entirely by the fire.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 15:5 teach us about usefulness and transformation after trials?
options: The vine tree becomes more useful after being burned
The vine tree was never fit for work, and even less so after being burned
After burning, the vine tree is fit for making pins
The vine tree is transformed into a strong tool
questions.correctAnswer: The vine tree was never fit for work, and even less so after being burned
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:5 explains that the vine tree was originally not fit for any work, and after being consumed by fire, it is even less suitable, emphasizing the idea of loss of usefulness after judgment or trial.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 15:6 use the analogy of the vine tree to describe the fate of Jerusalem's inhabitants?
options: They will grow strong and fruitful like the vine tree
They will be given to the fire as fuel just like the vine tree
They will be protected like the vine tree in the forest
They will be planted and nourished like the vine tree
questions.correctAnswer: They will be given to the fire as fuel just like the vine tree
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:6 compares the inhabitants of Jerusalem to the vine tree given to the fire for fuel, indicating that just as the vine tree is consumed, so will the inhabitants face judgment and destruction.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 15:7 say will happen when God sets His face against the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
options: They will find peace and restoration
They will go out from one fire to another, being devoured
They will become fruitful and prosperous
They will be hidden and protected from harm
questions.correctAnswer: They will go out from one fire to another, being devoured
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:7 describes that when God sets His face against Jerusalem’s inhabitants, they will experience continual judgment, moving from one fire to another, symbolizing ongoing destruction.

questions.question: What is the main reason given in Ezekiel 15:8 for making the land desolate?
options: Because they built idols
Because they committed a trespass
Because they refused to plant vineyards
Because they trusted in wood instead of God
questions.correctAnswer: Because they committed a trespass
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:8 clearly states that the land will be made desolate because the inhabitants have committed a trespass, indicating sin and disobedience as the cause of judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 15:3 asks if wood taken from the vine tree is suitable for making a pin to hang a vessel upon.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:3 questions whether wood from the vine tree can be used for any work, specifically if men would take a pin from it to hang vessels, illustrating the vine’s lack of usefulness.

questions.question: Based on Ezekiel 15:4 and 15:5, what practical lesson can believers learn about trust and usefulness in God’s work?
options: Like the vine tree, we should be flexible and adaptable
If we are not useful before trials, we can become useful after them
Being unfruitful leads to loss of usefulness and judgment
Trials always make us more useful in God’s work
questions.correctAnswer: Being unfruitful leads to loss of usefulness and judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4 and 15:5 emphasize that the unfruitful vine tree was never suitable for work and becomes even less so after fire, teaching believers that fruitfulness and faithfulness are essential to remain useful and avoid judgment.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 15:6 imply about God's judgment and the consequences of disobedience?
options: Judgment is slow and forgiving
Judgment is like a fire consuming useless wood
Disobedience will be rewarded with prosperity
God will protect those who are unfruitful
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment is like a fire consuming useless wood
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:6 uses the image of the vine tree given to the fire to illustrate that God’s judgment consumes those who are unfruitful and disobedient, similar to fire consuming useless wood.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 15:7, what will the people of Jerusalem learn when God sets His face against them?
options: They will understand God's mercy
They will know that He is the LORD
They will become strong and fruitful
They will be hidden from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: They will know that He is the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:7 states that when God sets His face against them and they undergo judgment, they will know that He is the LORD, indicating that judgment reveals God's sovereignty.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 15:2 compares the vine tree to a branch among the forest trees to highlight its superiority.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:2 asks what the vine tree is more than any other tree or branch, implying it is not superior but is being questioned for its lack of usefulness compared to other trees.

questions.question: If a believer feels unproductive and discouraged, how does Ezekiel 15:4-5 encourage understanding about usefulness?
options: That only fruitful believers are valuable to God
That all believers are equally useful regardless of fruitfulness
That usefulness can be restored after failure
That fruitlessness results in being consumed or wasted
questions.correctAnswer: That fruitlessness results in being consumed or wasted
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4-5 shows that the vine tree, being unfruitful, is useless and consumed by fire, teaching that fruitlessness leads to loss and judgment, encouraging believers to be fruitful and faithful.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 15:8 teach about the consequences of trespass or sin?
options: It leads to land making desolate
It results in mercy and restoration
It brings blessings and prosperity
It causes the vine tree to flourish
questions.correctAnswer: It leads to land making desolate
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:8 explicitly states the land will be made desolate because of trespass, illustrating the serious consequences of sin and disobedience.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 15:3 emphasize the practical uselessness of the vine tree?
options: By showing it can be used to make furniture
By questioning if men would take even a pin from it to hang vessels
By describing its strong and durable wood
By stating it is the most useful tree in the forest
questions.correctAnswer: By questioning if men would take even a pin from it to hang vessels
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:3 asks rhetorically if the vine tree’s wood is fit even for a small use like a pin to hang vessels, emphasizing its lack of practical value.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 15:1 introduces the chapter with the word of the LORD coming to Ezekiel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:1 states that the word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel, setting the stage for the message that follows.

questions.question: What practical spiritual truth can be drawn from Ezekiel 15:4-6 about faithfulness?
options: Faithfulness guarantees no trials
Unfaithfulness leads to judgment just as useless wood is consumed by fire
Trials always strengthen faithfulness
God rewards unfruitfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Unfaithfulness leads to judgment just as useless wood is consumed by fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4-6 uses the metaphor of the vine tree being consumed by fire to show that unfaithfulness and fruitlessness lead to divine judgment, encouraging believers to live faithfully.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 15.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 15, what is the primary use of the vine tree wood as described in the chapter?
options: To make tools
To hang vessels
To be cast into the fire for fuel
To build houses
questions.correctAnswer: To be cast into the fire for fuel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4 explains that the vine tree wood is cast into the fire for fuel, where it is burned and devoured, indicating its primary use as fuel rather than for making tools or other purposes.

questions.question: What does God say He will do to the inhabitants of Jerusalem in comparison to the vine tree among the trees of the forest?
options: He will protect them like the vine tree
He will give them as fuel to the fire
He will bless them with fruitfulness
He will make them rulers over the forest
questions.correctAnswer: He will give them as fuel to the fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:6 likens the inhabitants of Jerusalem to the vine tree given to the fire for fuel, indicating that God will give them over to destruction as the vine wood is given to the fire.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 15:7, what is the significance of the phrase, 'they shall go out from one fire, and another fire shall devour them'?
options: It represents their escape from danger
It symbolizes continuous judgment and destruction
It illustrates their purification process
It describes their triumph over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes continuous judgment and destruction
questions.explanation: The phrase in Ezekiel 15:7 indicates that the inhabitants will face ongoing judgment and destruction, moving from one calamity to another, showing God's displeasure and judgment upon them.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Ezekiel 15:8 for God making the land desolate?
options: Because of their idolatry
Because they have committed a trespass
Because of famine and drought
Because of foreign invasion
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have committed a trespass
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:8 clearly states that the land will be made desolate because the people have committed a trespass, indicating their sin and disobedience as the cause.

questions.question: What rhetorical question does God ask about the vine tree in Ezekiel 15:2?
options: Why does the vine tree bear fruit?
What is the vine tree more than any tree in the forest?
How long does the vine tree live?
Who planted the vine tree in the forest?
questions.correctAnswer: What is the vine tree more than any tree in the forest?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:2 contains the question, 'What is the vine tree more than any tree, or than a branch which is among the trees of the forest?' emphasizing the vine's insignificance compared to other trees.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 15:5 describe the vine tree's usefulness when whole and after being burned?
options: Useful for building houses when whole, useless when burned
Useful for making tools when burned, useless when whole
Not useful for any work either whole or burned
Valuable as fuel both whole and burned
questions.correctAnswer: Not useful for any work either whole or burned
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:5 explains that the vine tree was not fit for any work even when whole; therefore, it is even less fit after being burned.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of judgment by fire similar to Ezekiel 15:7?
options: Isaiah 66:15
Genesis 1:1
Psalm 23:1
Proverbs 3:5
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 66:15
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:15 speaks of the LORD coming with fire to execute judgment, paralleling Ezekiel 15:7 where fire symbolizes divine judgment upon Jerusalem.

questions.question: What literary device is predominantly used in Ezekiel 15 to describe Jerusalem’s inhabitants?
options: Parable
Allegory
Metaphor
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15 uses the metaphor of the vine tree wood being useless and burned as a symbol for the inhabitants of Jerusalem being given over to destruction, as seen throughout the chapter.

questions.question: In the original Hebrew, the word translated as 'trespass' in Ezekiel 15:8 is 'pesha'. What does this term primarily imply?
options: A minor error or mistake
A deliberate rebellion or revolt against God
A ceremonial impurity
An accidental sin
questions.correctAnswer: A deliberate rebellion or revolt against God
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'pesha' used in Ezekiel 15:8 connotes a willful rebellion against God's covenant, emphasizing the intentional nature of the people's sin.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 15 portrays the vine tree as more valuable than other trees in the forest.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:2 questions what the vine tree is more than any other tree, implying it is not more valuable, and verses 4-5 show it is not fit for work, reinforcing its lesser value.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 15:7 states that God will set His face against the people so that they will recognize Him as the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:7 declares that when God sets His face against the people and they experience judgment, they will know that He is the LORD, confirming His sovereignty and justice.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of destructive judgment found in Ezekiel 15:7-8?
options: Revelation 20:9
Matthew 3:10
John 3:16
Romans 8:28
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 3:10
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:10 uses the image of trees being cut down and cast into fire as judgment, echoing Ezekiel 15:7-8’s theme of destructive judgment by fire.

questions.question: Ezekiel 15:1 introduces the chapter by stating, 'And the word of the LORD came unto me.' What does this phrase indicate about the nature of the message?
options: It is a historical narrative
It is a personal opinion of Ezekiel
It is a divine revelation given to the prophet
It is a parable told by Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: It is a divine revelation given to the prophet
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:1 indicates that the message is a direct communication from God to Ezekiel, marking it as divine revelation rather than human opinion or narrative.

questions.question: How does the theme of uselessness of the vine wood in Ezekiel 15 relate to Israel’s covenant unfaithfulness as depicted elsewhere in Ezekiel?
options: It symbolizes Israel’s strength and durability
It represents Israel’s fruitfulness in obedience
It illustrates Israel’s unproductive and corrupt state due to sin
It signifies Israel’s victory over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates Israel’s unproductive and corrupt state due to sin
questions.explanation: The metaphor in Ezekiel 15 of the vine wood’s uselessness parallels Israel’s failure to produce righteousness and faithfulness, as also seen in Ezekiel 16 and 23 where Israel’s spiritual corruption leads to judgment.

questions.question: Which historical and cultural context helps us understand the significance of fire as a symbol in Ezekiel 15:4-7?
options: Fire was seen as a cleansing agent in ancient Near Eastern rituals
Fire was used as a symbol of royal coronation
Fire was only used for cooking and had no symbolic meaning
Fire represented prosperity and blessing
questions.correctAnswer: Fire was seen as a cleansing agent in ancient Near Eastern rituals
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, fire often symbolized purification and judgment, which helps explain Ezekiel 15:4-7’s use of fire to represent God’s purifying and punishing action against Jerusalem’s inhabitants.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What question does God ask Ezekiel about the vine tree in comparison with other trees?
options: What is the vine tree more than any tree or a branch among the forest trees?
Why does the vine tree produce fruit unlike other trees?
Is the vine tree the tallest among the forest trees?
Can the vine tree be used to build houses like other trees?
questions.correctAnswer: What is the vine tree more than any tree or a branch among the forest trees?
questions.explanation: God asks in Ezekiel 15:2 what the vine tree is more than any other tree or branch among the forest trees, highlighting the vine's relative insignificance for woodwork.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 15, what is the primary use of the wood from the vine tree?
options: To be cast into the fire for fuel
To build furniture
To make pegs for hanging vessels
To craft tools
questions.correctAnswer: To be cast into the fire for fuel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4 states that the wood of the vine tree is cast into the fire for fuel, as it is not suitable for crafting or structural work.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 15:3 suggest about the suitability of vine wood for making pins to hang vessels?
options: It is not suitable for making pins
It is highly suitable and durable
It is the preferred wood for pins
It is occasionally used for pins
questions.correctAnswer: It is not suitable for making pins
questions.explanation: Verse 3 questions if men would take a pin from vine wood to hang vessels, implying it is unsuitable for such use.

questions.question: What does the burning of the vine wood illustrate about the inhabitants of Jerusalem in this chapter?
options: They will be given to fire for judgment
They will be preserved like fine wood
They will be made fruitful and strong
They will be used to build the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They will be given to fire for judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:6 uses the metaphor of the vine wood given to the fire to symbolize the inhabitants of Jerusalem being given over to judgment and destruction.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily revealed by God's declaration in Ezekiel 15:7 to set His face against the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
options: God's justice and righteous judgment
God's mercy and forgiveness
God's omniscience
God's omnipotence
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and righteous judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:7 reveals God's attribute of justice as He sets His face against Jerusalem, bringing judgment upon them for their trespasses.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by Ezekiel 15:5 when stating the wood is unfit for work before and after burning?
options: Doctrine of human depravity and worthlessness apart from God
Doctrine of sanctification and usefulness in God’s service
Doctrine of resurrection and renewal
Doctrine of election and predestination
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of human depravity and worthlessness apart from God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:5 teaches that just as the vine wood is unfit for work, humans are spiritually unfit and worthless apart from God’s grace, illustrating total depravity.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 15:8 connect to the broader redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: It shows the consequence of sin as desolation, echoing Fall and exile themes
It emphasizes the promise of restoration and new covenant
It describes the kingdom of God fully established
It foretells the coming of the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the consequence of sin as desolation, echoing Fall and exile themes
questions.explanation: Verse 8 connects to the broader biblical theme of sin leading to desolation and exile, reflecting humanity’s fall and the need for redemption.

questions.question: What synthesis of Ezekiel 15:4 and 15:5 provides a theological insight into the nature of judgment?
options: Judgment consumes and utterly renders the sinner unfit for service
Judgment purifies and prepares for future usefulness
Judgment is temporary and reversible
Judgment only affects external behavior
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment consumes and utterly renders the sinner unfit for service
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 together teach that like the vine wood consumed by fire and rendered useless, divine judgment utterly consumes sinners, making them unfit for any good work.

questions.question: What theological lesson does the comparison of the vine tree to other forest trees in Ezekiel 15:2-3 teach about human self-worth?
options: Human worth is not inherent but based on God’s purpose and use
All humans have equal inherent worth regardless of behavior
Humans are superior to all creation by default
Self-worth is determined by societal status
questions.correctAnswer: Human worth is not inherent but based on God’s purpose and use
questions.explanation: God’s questioning in verses 2-3 about the vine tree’s inferiority teaches that worth depends on God’s purpose, not inherent qualities, reflecting human spiritual condition.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 15:6-7 contribute to understanding the attribute of God’s holiness?
options: God’s holiness demands judgment upon sinning Jerusalem
God’s holiness is only about love and acceptance
God’s holiness ignores human sin
God’s holiness is not related to judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands judgment upon sinning Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 show that God’s holiness is incompatible with sin, leading Him to set His face against Jerusalem and bring judgment, underscoring the holiness attribute.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Ezekiel 15:7 and Ezekiel 15:8 convey about divine judgment and its consequences?
options: God’s judgment results in desolation as a consequence of trespass
God’s judgment always leads to immediate restoration
God’s judgment is symbolic and has no real effect
God’s judgment is selective and does not affect the land
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment results in desolation as a consequence of trespass
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 together teach that God’s judgment upon Jerusalem for trespass leads to desolation of the land, revealing the serious consequences of sin.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's judgment is arbitrary and unjust. What does Ezekiel 15:6-8 actually teach about God's judgment?
options: God’s judgment is purposeful, righteous, and a response to human trespass
God judges without reason or warning
God’s judgment is inflicted on the innocent
God’s judgment is based on favoritism
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is purposeful, righteous, and a response to human trespass
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:6-8 demonstrates that God’s judgment is deliberate and just, responding to Jerusalem’s trespass and resulting in desolation, affirming divine righteousness.

questions.question: What narrative arc does Ezekiel 15:1-2 initiate in the chapter regarding God's communication with Ezekiel?
options: God reveals a metaphor to explain judgment using the vine tree
God promises restoration through a vine tree
God announces a new covenant through Ezekiel
God recalls the creation of the forest
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals a metaphor to explain judgment using the vine tree
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 begin with God speaking to Ezekiel, introducing the vine tree metaphor to illustrate the forthcoming judgment on Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the image of the vine wood being consumed by fire in Ezekiel 15:4-6?
options: Doctrine of divine judgment and human accountability
Doctrine of grace and forgiveness
Doctrine of eternal security
Doctrine of predestination without human responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of divine judgment and human accountability
questions.explanation: The metaphor of the vine wood burned by fire in verses 4-6 highlights divine judgment and human accountability for sin.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from synthesizing Ezekiel 15:3 and Ezekiel 15:5 about human usefulness before God?
options: Humans are inherently unfit for good works without God's intervention
Humans are naturally fit for all good works
Human usefulness is guaranteed regardless of condition
Humans determine their own worth by works alone
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are inherently unfit for good works without God's intervention
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 5 together teach that like the vine wood unsuitable for work, humans apart from God's grace are unfit for good works.
